author: Claude
note: Reference template. Two predicates worked through completely so every other group file has an unambiguous model to follow. bars[0] is the REFERENCE (most recently closed) bar; index increases going back in time. Bars are [open, high, low, close, tick_volume].

conventions.index_direction: bars[0] = reference bar, bars[1] = one bar older, ...
conventions.expected_derivation: positive/negative cases must be derived from what the pattern IS, never from reading the source thresholds. Only boundary cases may cite a source threshold, and must declare basis=implementation_threshold.
conventions.floating_point: NEVER place a boundary fixture exactly ON a threshold. Double arithmetic makes exact equality unreliable (e.g. 100.2 - 100.0 = 0.19999999999999574, which is NOT equal to 0.10 * 2.0). Write one fixture clearly INSIDE the threshold and one clearly OUTSIDE it, with at least ~5% margin, and state which side it is on.
conventions.filler_series: Optional list of bars cycled to reach the predicate's required window length. Use it for long-window predicates so the fixture stays readable; make sure the filler does not accidentally create the pattern.
conventions.anchor_date: Optional date of bars[0] (YYYY-MM-DD). Only the calendar predicates read bar timestamps; everything else can leave it at the default.
conventions.default_filler_series: Group-level padding, cycled to reach each predicate's required window. Every predicate needs at least 3 bars even when it only reads bar[0], so this keeps single-bar fixtures readable. Override per fixture when the padding is itself under test.

fixtures.rationale: A doji is a candle whose open and close are effectively equal, so the session ended undecided after ranging in both directions. Open 100.00 vs close 100.02 on a 2.00 range is exactly that: a body of 1% of the range.
The opposite of undecided: the candle opens at its low and closes near its high, spending 90% of its range on directional body. No trader would read this as a doji.

Body is 0.18 on a range of 2.00 = 9% of range, comfortably inside the 10%-of-range body ceiling the implementation declares. Deliberately not placed exactly on 10%: double arithmetic cannot be trusted at equality.
Body is 0.22 on a range of 2.00 = 11% of range, clearly outside the 10% ceiling. Paired with the inside case this brackets the threshold from both directions without relying on exact float equality.

A hammer is a small body sitting at the top of the range with a long lower shadow and almost no upper shadow: price was driven far down and fully rejected. Body 0.50, lower wick 4.50 (9x the body), upper wick 0.10.

Same small body, but the long shadow is on the WRONG side: a 5.00 upper wick and a 0.10 lower wick. This is the shape of upside rejection, the mirror image of a hammer, and must not be reported as one.
Body 0.50, upper wick 0.14 = 28% of the body, inside the 30%-of-body upper-wick ceiling. Lower wick and body-to-range stay comfortably valid so this fixture isolates the upper-wick condition alone.
Identical to the inside case except the upper wick is 0.16 = 32% of the body, outside the 30% ceiling. The single changed value isolates which condition rejected the candle.
